name: Physics
description: The natural science of matter, energy, and the fundamental laws that govern the universe
author: Techdoc

words.definition: A push or pull that can change motion.

contextSentences.en: Four fundamental forces govern the universe: gravity, electromagnetism, and the strong and weak nuclear forces.
The unit of force in the International System of Units is the newton, named after Isaac Newton.

words.example_en: In physics, force can make a stationary ball start moving.
words.example_sk: Vo fyzike môže sila spôsobiť, že sa nehybná lopta začne pohybovať.

words.definition: The amount of matter in an object.

contextSentences.en: Mass is a scalar quantity measured in kilograms and remains constant regardless of location.
Einstein's famous equation E = mc² shows that mass is a concentrated form of energy.

words.example_en: The bowling ball has more mass than the tennis ball.
words.example_sk: Bowlingová guľa má väčšiu hmotnosť ako tenisová loptička.

words.definition: The speed of something in a particular direction.

contextSentences.en: Nothing in the universe can travel faster than the velocity of light in a vacuum.
The velocity of sound in air at 20 °C is approximately 343 metres per second.

words.example_en: The rocket's velocity increased as it left the launch pad.
words.example_sk: Rýchlosť rakety sa zvýšila, keď opustila štartovaciu rampu.

words.definition: The rate at which velocity changes over time.

contextSentences.en: At the LHC, particles are brought to nearly the speed of light through rapid acceleration.
A free-falling object in a vacuum provides a perfect example of uniform acceleration.

words.example_en: The car's acceleration pushed us back into our seats.
words.example_sk: Zrýchlenie auta nás zatlačilo do sedadiel.

words.definition: The quantity of motion of a moving body.

contextSentences.en: The law of conservation of momentum states that the total momentum of a closed system remains constant.
In a collision, momentum is transferred from one object to another.

words.example_en: The truck's momentum carried it forward even after the driver braked.
words.example_sk: Vďaka zotrvačnosti sa nákladné auto pohybovalo dopredu aj po tom, čo vodič zabrzdil.

words.definition: The force that resists motion between surfaces.

contextSentences.en: Without friction, it would be impossible to walk because your feet would slip on the ground.
Rolling friction is generally lower than sliding friction, which is why wheels are so efficient.

words.example_en: Friction between the tires and the road helps the car stop.
words.example_sk: Trenie medzi pneumatikami a vozovkou pomáha vozidlu zabrzdiť.

words.definition: A disturbance that transfers energy through space or matter.

contextSentences.en: Light is an electromagnetic wave and does not need a medium to travel through.
The double-slit experiment produced a classic interference pattern, proving the wave nature of light.

words.example_en: A huge wave crashed onto the shore during the storm.
words.example_sk: Počas búrky sa na breh zvalila obrovská vlna.

words.definition: The number of repeated events in a given time.

contextSentences.en: The frequency of alternating current in Europe is 50 hertz.
Ultrasound has a frequency above 20 kHz and cannot be heard by the human ear.

words.example_en: The radio station changed its frequency to avoid interference.
words.example_sk: Rádiová stanica zmenila frekvenciu, aby sa vyhla rušeniu.

words.definition: The smallest possible amount of a physical quantity.

contextSentences.en: Max Planck introduced the concept of the quantum in 1900 to explain blackbody radiation.
A photon is the quantum of light and carries a specific amount of energy.

words.example_en: Quantum theory explains how particles behave at very small scales.
words.example_sk: Kvantová teória vysvetľuje, ako sa častice správajú v mimoriadne malých rozmeroch.

words.definition: A very small piece of matter.

contextSentences.en: The Higgs particle was experimentally confirmed at the CERN accelerator in 2012.
Alpha particles consist of two protons and two neutrons and are emitted during radioactive decay.

words.example_en: A dust particle floated through the sunlight by the window.
words.example_sk: Častica prachu sa vznášala v slnečnom svetle pri okne.

words.definition: The central part of an atom.

contextSentences.en: The diameter of an atomic nucleus is about 100,000 times smaller than that of the whole atom.
In nuclear fusion, two light nuclei merge into a heavier one and release large amounts of energy.

words.example_en: The nucleus of the atom contains protons and neutrons.
words.example_sk: Jadro atómu obsahuje protóny a neutróny.

words.definition: Energy transmitted through waves or particles.

contextSentences.en: X-ray radiation is used in medicine to make internal body structures visible.
Cosmic radiation constantly bombards the Earth's atmosphere, creating secondary particles.

words.example_en: The doctor limited the patient's radiation exposure during the scan.
words.example_sk: Lekár obmedzil ožiarenie pacienta počas vyšetrenia.

words.definition: The study of heat, energy, and work.

contextSentences.en: The second law of thermodynamics states that the entropy of a closed system never decreases.
Thermodynamics plays a central role in the design of heat engines such as steam turbines.

words.example_en: Thermodynamics helps engineers design more efficient engines.
words.example_sk: Termodynamika pomáha inžinierom navrhovať účinnejšie motory.

words.definition: The opposition to electric current or motion.

contextSentences.en: Ohm's Law describes the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance in a circuit.
Superconductors have an electrical resistance of exactly zero at certain temperatures.

words.example_en: The wire's resistance increased as its temperature rose.
words.example_sk: S rastúcou teplotou sa zvyšoval odpor drôtu.

words.definition: A state in which opposing forces are balanced.

contextSentences.en: A body is in static equilibrium when the sum of all forces and torques acting on it is zero.
Thermal equilibrium is reached when two objects in contact reach the same temperature.

words.example_en: The gymnast maintained equilibrium on the narrow balance beam.
words.example_sk: Gymnastka udržala rovnováhu na úzkej kladine.
